links.outcome: Patient moral blame of physician after adverse outcome, by adherence to GAI advice
links.effect: Physicians who adhered to GAI advice incurred significantly less moral blame than those who did not (p < 0.001). The effect was stronger for personalized regimens (p < 0.001) than for standard-of-care (p < 0.05).
links.quote: The analysis shows a significant diffusion of responsibility i.e., when an adverse outcome occurs, physicians who adhere to GAI advice incur significantly less moral blame than those who do not (p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Diffusion of accountability from physician to GAI in patient blame judgments
links.effect: Adherence to GAI advice significantly reduced moral blame directed at the physician (p < 0.001), most strongly for personalized treatment. This is consistent with diffusion of accountability.
links.quote: The analysis shows a significant diffusion of responsibility i.e., when an adverse outcome occurs, physicians who adhere to GAI advice incur significantly less moral blame than those who do not (p < 0.001).

screen.reason: Vignette-based experiment evaluating patient moral judgments and diffusion of responsibility when physicians adhere vs. do not adhere to generative AI advice.
